attribution_limitations: The text describes a first re-exploration on the day congestion appeared, with multiple venous anastomotic thrombi, followed by three additional explorations over the subsequent 48 hours; Table 4 (Appendix D) logs four re-explorations on POD 3 and POD 4, the first with multiple intraluminal venous thrombi. The counts and findings are consistent, but the source does not literally map each text exploration to a table row, so text and table items are kept separate. The Table 4 legend says times are in 24-hour format, yet the rows give only day-part labels.

The 4Ts sentence says the score supported cessation of all heparin products and initiation of non-heparin anticoagulation; the Discussion says the score justified early alternative anticoagulation in hindsight; the limitations list absent timestamps for the initiation of non-heparin anticoagulation, which presupposes initiation without stating it. No sentence states that heparin was stopped or that a named non-heparin anticoagulant was given, or when.

The abstract orders the positive anti-PF4/heparin result after the platelet fall and 4Ts assessment ("subsequently") and does not place it relative to death; the Discussion says the test "later returned positive" in the sentence after the death sentence, without naming its anchor. Neither passage literally states the result before or after death, so this is not recorded as a source conflict and no relation to death is asserted.

The source names free flap loss only through the Discussion phrase that findings are consistent with HIT as the proximate cause of free flap loss; the loss event itself, its date and its basis are not described.

Table 1 states that abnormal values are emphasized and gives reference intervals, but the text of the table carries no flags; the source calls no individual laboratory value high or low except through the platelet statements.
